smoking_behavior.quit_intention: Will quit in the next month

rated_messages.input_message: Notice how stress and anxiety may pull you and make you want to smoke. Just notice this. You can choose to just notice and not smoke.
Ways of dealing with urges: play a game or an online quiz.
Tell yourself, “I am going to quit smoking soon.” Say it out loud. Say to yourself, “I am too strong to continue smoking for the rest of my life."
You were often stressed in this location and this might trigger urges. What can you do to reduce your stress here? If you can avoid this place until things settle down, then do.
Stress is temporary. It comes and goes like passing clouds in the sky. When stress demands you to light up, remember you can let it pass by without smoking.
Step back from what is stressful by taking 10 slow breaths. Count them as you go and notice your breath. If you get distracted, keep starting over until you get to 10.
Picture the people or things you care deeply about. On a scale of 0-10, how willing are you to let this urge pass for those reasons?
When you are stressed, it is easy to focus on the things that are going wrong. Take a few moments to focus on 5 things that have gone well or that you are thankful for this week.
Acknowledge your unhelpful thought by writing it down on a piece of paper. Then let it be on it's way by crumpling it up and tossing it in a trash can.
Imagine this urge as just another backseat passenger that hopped in after seeing other people smoke. You are the driver and you still get to call the shots.
